text:
rachel: Heads-up from morning traces: p95 host parse jumped after we enabled slice-coalescer/stitcher on edge. spike ~13% on 64-128 token wallet of requests.
diego: stack top: parse_stitch -> chunk_reassemble -> tokenize_incremental -> kvcache_lookup.
sam: grpc vs http1 numbers?
rachel: grpc p95 host parse 1.6ms, http1 2.9ms in the window. coalescer reduces network calls but is creating mixed-length micro-batches.
diego: kernel_selector logs show many switches to "conservative-fallback" for batches with seq-stddev > 4.0. the stitcher frequently merges a 6-token chat with a 256-token longform doc.
nina: KV counters: per-batch lookups +22%, kvcache miss +3.1%, eviction bursts aligned with host parse tail.sam: sounds like a feedback loop: mixed batches -> conservative kernel -> higher CPU -> longer preproc -> more batching backlog -> worse mixing.
rachel: quick proposals: 1) have stitcher avoid merging when estimated seq variance > threshold (cheap histogram compare), 2) clamp variance in kernel selection by clipping extremes (e.g., cap lengths at p95 for calc), 3) tokenization micro-optimizations (pre-reserve, ascii fastpath).
diego: implementation notes: pre-reserve cut tokenize_incremental median from 0.42ms -> 0.15ms in microbench. ascii fastpath saves ~0.12ms for ascii-heavy payloads. both behind flags.
nina: affinity idea: short routing affinity window so repeated requests from same user hit same kvcache shard, reduces cross-shard lookups. sim dropped eviction spike by ~38%, but needs TTL tuning.sam: http1 smallwrite problem persists. suggest enabling header-frag coalesce at ingress and prefer h2 for internal calls.
ops-bot: ticket PERF-7902 created: "microfragment stitcher + host-parse tail" assigned to rachel, diego, nina.
rachel: runbook actions: A) add stitcher skip-on-high-variance (rachel), B) kernel-variance-clamp flag (diego), C) pre-reserve + ascii path PR (sam), D) affinity experiment (nina), E) ingress header-coalesce toggle (infra).
diego: will add metric "stitcher_mixed_batch_rate" + "kernel_mispredict_rate" to p95 dashboard.
sam: note on memory: pre-reserve must use pooled slabs with per-worker cap to avoid RSS blowups on dense hosts. add cap param.
nina: I'll schedule affinity for 5% canary with eviction dashboards.
rachel: target: land patches behind flags in 48h, canary runs for 24-48h, measure host_parse_p95 and kvcache_eviction_spikes.
diego: thumbs up. if host_parse_p95 drops under 1.2ms for small requests we expect ~6% overall tail reduction.
ops-bot: remind: include flame traces and microbench artifacts in PRs.
rachel: will attach traces. thanks team :rocket:
